# GroupDocs.Parser MCP Server

MCP server for GroupDocs.Parser — extract text, images, metadata, tables, and barcodes from documents via AI agents. Wraps GroupDocs.Parser for .NET and exposes it as tool calls for Claude, Cursor, VS Code / GitHub Copilot, and other MCP-compatible clients. Supports PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, HTML, EPUB, MSG, EML, JPG, PNG, TIFF, and 50+ more document and image formats. Exposes extract_text, extract_images, extract_metadata, extract_tables, extract_barcodes, get_document_info, and get_license_status tools.

## Install

Docker-first product - the packed tool exceeds NuGet.org's 250 MB limit, so there is no dnx / NuGet path. Multi-arch image (amd64 + arm64) on GHCR only; pin by replacing :latest with a version tag.

- As a Docker container: `docker run --rm -i -v $(pwd)/documents:/data ghcr.io/groupdocs-parser/parser-net-mcp:latest`

## MCP tools

- extract_text — extract plain text from a document (whole or per page). Truncates large outputs.
- extract_images — save embedded images to storage as `<basename>_image<N>.<ext>` files; returns a saved-path list.
- extract_metadata — author / title / dates / EXIF / XMP / IPTC / custom properties as JSON.
- extract_tables — tables as Markdown (default — renders in chat) or structured JSON (`format='json'`).
- extract_barcodes — decoded values + types + page + confidence + angle for each barcode / QR code found.
- get_document_info — file type + page count + size as JSON, without modifying the file.
- get_license_status — active licensing mode (evaluation / licensed / metered), engine version, and metered consumption. Takes no arguments and processes no document.

## Supported formats

PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, ODT, RTF, HTML, EPUB, MSG, EML, JPG, PNG, TIFF, BMP, GIF, MP3, MP4, and 50+ other document, image, and media formats.

## Environment variables

- GROUPDOCS_MCP_STORAGE_PATH — base folder for input + output (defaults to current working directory)
- GROUPDOCS_MCP_OUTPUT_PATH — optional, routes output files (used by extract_images) to a separate folder
- GROUPDOCS_LICENSE_PATH — path to a GroupDocs license file inside the container (GroupDocs.Parser.lic or GroupDocs.Total.lic); omit for evaluation mode; ignored when metered keys are set
- GROUPDOCS_METERED_PUBLIC_KEY — metered (pay-per-use) public key; needs the private key too and takes precedence over GROUPDOCS_LICENSE_PATH
- GROUPDOCS_METERED_PRIVATE_KEY — metered private key; secret, pass from the environment rather than a committed config

## Licensing

The MCP server is MIT; the underlying GroupDocs.Parser engine requires a license for production use. Evaluation mode (no license) truncates extraction silently: only the first 1,600 characters and 20 lines of text per file, only the first 5 pages/sheets/slides, 20 spreadsheet rows, 5 metadata properties per file, 100 files per session, plus evaluation marks — see https://docs.groupdocs.com/parser/net/evaluation-limitations-and-licensing/. Two ways to license: a license file (mount it into the container and set GROUPDOCS_LICENSE_PATH) or metered pay-per-use (set GROUPDOCS_METERED_PUBLIC_KEY and GROUPDOCS_METERED_PRIVATE_KEY; metered wins over a license file and needs outbound connectivity because usage is reported to GroupDocs servers). Call get_license_status to see the active mode and metered consumption. Free 30-day temporary license: https://purchase.groupdocs.com/temporary-license/ - purchase: https://purchase.groupdocs.com/pricing/parser/net

## Example prompts for AI agents

- "How many pages does invoice.pdf have, and what format is it?"
- "Extract the text from page 2 of contract.docx."
- "What's the author and creation date of report.xlsx?"
- "Pull the line items table out of invoice.pdf as Markdown."
- "Are there any QR codes in shipping-label.png? If so, what do they decode to?"
